_doc: Gerald Pike, Hon. Secretary of Sandown Golf Club. Nineteen in May 1973, caddying for his father, he saw the man in the yellow coat walk the ninth and he laughed at Colin Rudd's father in the bar that week. He has kept the minutes ever since and he has never been asked. Pompous, precise, and softer than he sounds.

open.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: Members and guests. It says so on the board, which I had repainted in April, so I know it is legible.
He's reading our shoes like a wine list.

passives.line: Honorary Secretary. Not Captain. The Captain gets the photograph on the wall. The Secretary gets the minutes, and keeps them, and that's the one you want.
He said April. He's precise about paint. A man this precise kept something precise in 1973, and he's kept it since.
He's bored. Nobody has asked him a question that wasn't about bar prices in twenty years. Ask him a real one and watch him stand up straighter.

options.text: We're from an office in West Virginia, Mr Pike. We're here about May 1973.
We're not here to play. We'd be terrible at it.
Two children were taken into a hut off your ninth fairway. You were nineteen.

menu.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: Well. Go on, then. I have the fixture list to type and it does not type itself, whatever the Captain thinks.

static.line: He laughed. He was there in '73 and he laughed at the boy's father. Say it before he does. Say it to his face.

options.text: The man on the ninth fairway. Tell us.
A club like this keeps minutes. A club like this has a man who keeps them beautifully.
Who laughed at Colin Rudd's father first? The committee, or you?
You wrote to the camp. You kept the reply. Show us the letter or the County Press gets item seven.
That's all for now, Mr Pike.

ninth.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: May 1973. I was nineteen and caddying for my father on the Saturday of the bank holiday, which one did, then, if one wanted the car on Sunday.

A man came over the fence at the brook end of the ninth. Yellow coat. Lifeboat yellow. A hatbox in one hand and a tent bag over his shoulder, and he walked the whole length of the fairway in front of a fourball as if he had a tee time.
Nobody said a word to him. One does not, on the Island. One writes to the committee. Which my father did, and I typed it, and that is the first thing I ever typed for this club.

passives.line: He's told this as a funny story for twenty years. It stopped being funny somewhere around the hatbox, and he's only just noticed.

options.text: Did you tell anyone besides the committee?
A hatbox. On a golf course.

told.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: The committee had the camp manager in for a drink. He was a large man with a great many teeth and a club tie he had no right to, and after the drink everybody agreed that it was nothing. High spirits. Entertainments staff.
The following week the Rudd boy's father came into the bar. I shall come to that if you make me, and not before.
He'll come to it, dear. Men like this always do. They've been rehearsing it longer than the camp rehearsed anything.

photo.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: Captain's Day, 1973. Second row, the boy in the blazer that doesn't fit: that is me. The blazer was my father's.
Front row, left of the Captain. The camp manager. A guest of the committee, that month of all months. I have never taken the photograph down and I could not tell you why.
That's a yellowcoat's boss if I ever saw one. Look at those teeth.

passives.line: Camp manager at Captain's Day, May 1973. A guest of the committee the same month the committee wrote to him. That's not a complaint. That's an arrangement.

minutes.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: ...Beautifully. Yes. Nobody has ever said that.

The fourth of June, 1973. Item seven. Complaint from members regarding Sunnyside Holiday Camp staff 'rehearsing' on the ninth fairway with a tent and paint. Letter to the camp manager. Matter closed on receipt of an apology and a donation to the roof fund.
The roof was done in 1974. It is a very good roof. I have always thought it a very good roof and I have never once enjoyed it.
Rehearsing. With a tent and paint. The week two children were taken into a hut.

minutes_no.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: The minutes are the property of the committee, and the committee meets on the first Tuesday, and you, I think, will be gone by then.
He wants to show us. He's just decided we haven't earned it yet. Come back when we've got something to put on his desk.

laughed.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: He came into the bar in his work boots, which one does not, and he asked whether any of the gentlemen had seen a man in a hat. And I said, which hat, we have all got hats. And the bar laughed. And he went out.
He never came in again. His son is twenty-eight and lives above the chemist and has never set foot on this course, and I have been Secretary for nineteen years and I have never once asked him to.

passives.line: Nineteen, in his father's blazer, and he got a laugh. He has been paying that laugh off in minutes ever since.

laughed_no.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: I do not recall who laughed. It was a bar. Bars laugh.
They do. Usually at whoever's just left.

softens.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: ...I kept the minutes, you know. All of them. Thirty years, every meeting, every item. Nobody reads them.
I rather hoped someone would. I rather hoped it would be someone who would ask about item seven, and not about the roof.
He's been waiting for us. Not for us. For anybody. We'll do.

letter.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: The County Press. Yes. You would, too. ...Under the blotter. Don't touch it, I shall read it.

'Dear Mr Pike. Our entertainments staff regret any alarm caused to junior persons on the Levels during a rehearsal for the Children's Carnival. The member of staff concerned has been spoken to. Please find enclosed a cheque toward the clubhouse roof.' June the eleventh, 1973. Signed by a man with a great many teeth.
Spoken to. Two children said a thing in a hat took them into a hut, and the whole Island read 'spoken to' and went back to the beach. I typed the envelope.
That's it. That's the case, under a blotter, for twenty-one years.

thrown_out.speaker: lv_secretary
lines: Terry! These people are not guests. Members and guests, it says, and they are neither, and they may take their shoes with them.
...Well. That's the stiff upper lip. We found it.
